Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's fourth quarter and full-year 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q4 and for the full year 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production levels averaging 315,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, reflecting disciplined growth across our core assets. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on emissions reduction targets, where we've made significant strides toward our net-zero ambitions, including a 28% drop in GHG intensity year-to-date. We remain focused on advancing our ESG initiatives while optimizing our portfolio for long-term value. Finally, we are taking steps to further enhance cost efficiencies and free cash flow generation through our Efficiency 2.0 playbook.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Raj Patel: Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a strong quarter and full year. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.8 billion in free cash flow and returned $900 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $3.2 billion in debt and $1.5 billion in cash.

Let me dive deeper into some key metrics starting with EBITDA, which came in at $1.4 billion for the quarter, reflecting a robust 22% year-over-year increase from roughly $1.15 billion in Q4 2023. On a full-year trailing twelve months basis, adjusted EBITDA now stands at $5.2 billion, up 18% from the prior period. This outperformance underscores the strength of our asset base, disciplined capital allocation, and operational resilience amid a volatile macro environment with WTI hovering around $72 per barrel.

The key drivers behind this uplift start with realized pricing, a major tailwind. Our blended realized price per barrel of oil equivalent reached $78.50 per BOE, a 17% improvement from $67.10 per BOE last year. This stemmed from stronger Brent crude averaging $82 per barrel during the quarter, up from $75 in Q4 '23, coupled with a favorable WTI-Brent spread of about $3 per barrel. Henry Hub prices held steady at $2.85 per million BTU, supporting our 35% gas mix, while NGL realizations climbed to $28 per barrel on robust Mont Belvieu fractionation spreads. Our hedging program was crucial, with 65% of oil production hedged at a $70 per barrel floor via collars and swaps, locking in around $150 million in additional EBITDA compared to an unhedged position.

Production volumes grew meaningfully, contributing to the EBITDA strength. Total production averaged 315,000 BOE per day in Q4, up 3% quarter-over-quarter from 305,000 BOE per day in Q3 and 15% year-over-year from 274,000 BOE per day in Q4 2023. Oil volumes hit 215,000 barrels per day, a 4% QoQ increase from 207,000 barrels per day and a 22% YoY jump from 176,000 barrels per day. This was led by our Permian Basin, where 45 new Delaware Basin wells came online in the Avalon shale, posting initial rates of 1,800 barrels per day per well, 20% above type curve thanks to 4,000 pounds of proppant per foot and diverter tech. Eagle Ford's Catarina field added 14,000 BOE per day from refracs, while Gulf of Mexico shelf ops stabilized at 38,000 BOE per day post-upgrades.

Gas volumes were 630,000 Mcf per day, or 105,000 BOE per day, roughly flat QoQ but up 2% YoY. We curtailed some Haynesville output to manage pricing but saw Permian associated gas surge 6% QoQ to 350,000 Mcf per day. These gains more than offset a modest cash operating cost rise to $18.50 per BOE from $17.20, due to 12% inflation in tubulars and sand. We countered with LOE dropping 5% to $8.10 per BOE via AI predictive maintenance, cutting Permian downtime 18% and extending ESP lives to 850 days. G&A fell 12% YoY to $50 million through optimizations post-Bakken divestiture.

U.S. onshore drove 75% of growth, with Permian D&C at $650 per foot. North Sea's Buzzard added output at low LOE, and Kurdistan held steady. This positions us for 50% FCF returns, a 4.2% dividend yield, $600 million buybacks, and $2.4 billion 2025 capex skewed to Permian.

Turning to operating expenses per BOE, a critical efficiency metric amid razor-thin margins and service inflation. Full-year 2024 OpEx per BOE was $10.45, a 12% improvement from $11.85 in 2023 and 22% below the $13.40 Q4 2022 peak from supply chain issues. Q4 came in at $9.80, beating guidance by $0.45 and topping Permian peers like Pioneer and Occidental at $11 to $13 blended.

Trend-wise, over five quarters: Q4 '23 at $10.95 with LOE $6.20, GPT $3.45, workover $1.30 on 285 MBOE per day; Q1 '24 $10.75, LOE $6.10, GPT $3.40, workover $1.25 at 292; Q2 $10.60, LOE $6.00, GPT $3.35, workover $1.25 at 298; Q3 $10.25, LOE $5.80, GPT $3.25, workover $1.20 at 305; Q4 $9.80, LOE $5.50, GPT $3.10, workover $1.20 at 315. LOE down 11% YoY on scale, GPT 10% on midstream deals amid 15% ethane spread drops, workovers fewer at 45 versus 62.

Permian at $8.90, down from $10.20, via water recycling cutting disposal 25%; Bakken $13.50 on winter ops; Gulf $18.20 non-recurring. Drivers: 10% volume growth diluting fixed costs by 40%; outpacing 6-8% inflation.

Our Efficiency 2.0 strategies: $45 million in digital tech like Halliburton's DecisionSpace 360 for 15% LOE cuts, 28% less downtime, IoT extending VRP lives to 620 days saving $2.50 per BOE; drone inspections cut headcount 12%. Supply chain: 70% 2025 contracts flat, $150 million proppant at $45 per ton, GPT savings $0.30 per BOE. Ops: D&C down 18% to $650 per foot with SimulFrac at 3.2 wells per squad, 65% water recycle. Hedging service inflation, divesting high-cost Bakken.

2025 guide $9.50 to $10.00 per BOE, 5-9% down, with electrification upside $0.40 savings; risks buffered.

I'll now turn to ESG, where we've committed to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2050 from 2020 baseline, 50% intensity cut by 2030, OGCI methane goals. YTD, GHG intensity down 28% to 13.1 kgCO2e per BOE from 18.2, beating 2025 target early. Q/Q down 4% on flaring and efficiency.

Methane: 0.12 tonnes per million BOE, 62% YTD drop from 0.32; GHGSat satellites fixed 1,200 leaks, Permian 95% monitored slashing venting 75%; North Sea <0.1%, Middle East drones. Flaring: 0.4% of gas, down from 1.2%, absolute 4.2 Bcf via Permian gathering, Nigeria recovery. CCUS: 2.1 MtCO2 captured, Polaris 1 Mtpa expanding, Barents 450,000 tonnes, blue H2.

U.S. Permian 0.3% flaring, frac electrification; North Sea 9.5 kgCO2e/BOE; Middle East improving. 15% 2025 capex to low-carbon, sustainability bonds save 25 bps, Cheniere green LNG deal. Q4 holds 26-28% cut.

Now, over to Tom for operational details.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Raj. On the operational front, we continue to execute effectively. Production details align with Raj's overview: 315,000 BOE per day total, with oil at 68% cut. The Permian led with new Delaware wells outperforming via ApexMax designs at 120 bpm fracs. Eagle Ford Pearsall up 5% QoQ on diverters, Bakken horizontals yielding 800 MBOE EURs. Gas held via curtailments and Permian surge. Decline rates at 7-8%, guiding Q1 2025 to 320-330,000 BOE per day. Cost reductions tie to OpEx trends, with pad efficiencies and water management crushing basin averages.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Carter: Good morning, team. Can you provide more detail on the OpEx per BOE trends and your cost management strategies going forward?

Raj Patel: Good morning, Brian. Happy to expand. As I detailed, the downward trajectory to $9.80 in Q4 reflects volume leverage, tech like DecisionSpace cutting downtime 28%, supply locks on proppant and services, SimulFrac efficiencies, and 65% water recycle. Permian-specific wins like Loving County recycling saved $1.2 million quarterly. For 2025, $9.50-$10.00 guide assumes 330 MBOE/d, with electrification on 40% of pads adding $0.40/BOE savings. We've buffered risks like Red Sea freight with $100 million reserves. This weaponizes costs for FCF in a $70-80 WTI world.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA drivers into 2025, especially with commodity volatility?

Raj Patel: Morning, Lisa. Key 2025 drivers mirror Q4: hedged pricing at $78 oil floor, 8-10% volume growth to 330 MBOE/d via Permian D&C 70% of $2.4 billion capex, continued LOE efficiencies from digital oilfield. G&A savings post-divestitures, midstream JVs keeping GPT flat. Upside from 40% unhedged on Brent $75-90, OPEC cuts. We're returning 50% FCF, targeting $2 billion+ EBITDA.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson: Could you please provide more color on ESG progress, particularly methane and flaring?

Raj Patel: Sure, Mark. Methane intensity at 0.12 t/mmBOE, 62% below baseline via GHGSat and Rockwell monitors on 95% Permian wells, avoiding 450,000 tCO2e. Flaring to 0.4%, Permian gathering at 92% capture, Nigeria 98%. CCUS at 2.1 Mt, Polaris expanding. Regional: North Sea best-in-class, GCC improving with Aramco electrification. Ties to sustainability bonds and green LNG premiums.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim: Thanks. More on production mix and QoQ/YoY changes?

Tom Reilly: Hi Sarah. Q4 total 315k BOE/d, +3% QoQ/+15% YoY; oil 215k bbl/d +4%/+22%; gas 105k BOE/d flat/+2%. Permian drove oil via 45 Delaware wells at 1,200 IP30 75% oil; Eagle Ford refracs; Bakken conversions. Gas Permian associated up 6%, Haynesville AI comps. Oil First strategy: 75% Q1 capex to oil plays, hedges 60% oil $78, 40% gas $2.80. 350k by 2027 goal.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q4 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy—driving production growth, slashing OpEx, boosting EBITDA, advancing ESG—and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
